newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper -- in sights of assassins.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper -- in sights of assassins.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper has been targeted for assassination more than 50 times since he took office in August 1994, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said on Friday.

It cited "government intelligence reports" as saying most of the 57 plots against Samper involved organised crime and leftist guerrillas. One involved the discovery of a powerful explosive that had been set to destroy most of the airport in the northeast city of Cucuta during Samper's recent visit.

Another would have involved a "hit" on the president during a visit he made in July to a guerrilla-infested region of central Tolima province, shortly after Washington revoked his U.S. travel visa because of his alleged ties to drug lords, El Espectador said.

It gave no other details but Samper, who has hailed the arrests and imprisonment of the same Cali drug cartel bosses who are accused of financing his presidential campaign, has no shortage of enemies at home and abroad.

He still carries four of the 11 bullets fired at him by right-wing hitmen at Bogota's international airport in March 1989 as he stood talking to a leftist political leader. He spent days in a coma and needed 22 operations to recover from the attack, which gave him a reputation as a thick-skinned politician with an uncanny instinct for survival.
